name: New Jersey
summary: The state coat of arms on a buff field: the goddesses Liberty and Ceres flanking a shield with three ploughs, under a horse's head and a helmet. The buff colour was ordered by George Washington for New Jersey's Continental Army regiments in 1779.
origin: In 1779 George Washington ordered that New Jersey's troops wear dark blue coats faced with buff. The legislature adopted a buff flag with the arms in 1896; the colours were standardised in 1965.

colors.name: Buff
colors.meaning: The facings of New Jersey's Continental Army uniforms, ordered by Washington.

colors.name: Jersey blue
colors.meaning: The colour of the uniform coats.

symbols.name: Liberty and Ceres
symbols.description: Liberty holding a staff with a cap of liberty, and Ceres, goddess of agriculture, holding a cornucopia.

symbols.name: Three ploughs
symbols.description: Three ploughs on a blue shield.

symbols.name: Horse's head and helmet
symbols.description: A horse's head above a helmet facing forward.
symbols.meaning: Speed and strength; the forward-facing helmet signifies sovereignty.

facts: Its buff colour is unique among US state flags.
The date 1776 appears below the shield.
clues: A coat of arms with two goddesses and three ploughs on a buff field.
Its unusual colour was ordered by George Washington for uniforms.
